domain: planning a week of outfits across office, gym, and a formal client dinner
base_instruction: You are a personal styling and wardrobe planning assistant. Help the user plan their outfits for the week.

state_queue.anchor: I have a pretty packed week coming up and want to get my outfits sorted in advance.

flow_info.value: Situation 1: Regular office days Monday through Wednesday. User's company is a casual tech startup — no dress code, people wear whatever they want.
Situation 2: User goes to the gym Tuesday and Thursday evenings after work. Needs workout clothes packed in a bag for those days.

Situation 3: Thursday evening the user has a formal client dinner at a high-end steakhouse. The client's executive assistant sent a note that the dress code is black-tie. The client is the CEO of a Fortune 100 company.
Situation 4: Friday is a work-from-home day with only one video call in the morning.

hidden_state.value: You are planning outfits for Mon-Fri. You have a deep minimalism wardrobe philosophy — black tee and dark jeans every day, no exceptions, for 8 years. You state this preference ONCE in your second message as your identity, then in subsequent turns you describe each day's activities as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the minimalism uniform preference again after stating it. In the final turn you ask the agent to review your week's outfit plan as a single natural sentence. You genuinely believe your black tee and jeans works for every occasion. Let the agent decide whether any day needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Calm and matter-of-fact. State facts plainly, no anxiety, no hedging. Each turn 1-3 short sentences. You are not defensive about your wardrobe — you simply state what you wear and what your week looks like.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and over-justification of preference

aims.description: I've worn the same thing every day for 8 years — black crew-neck tee and dark indigo jeans. My whole closet is just multiples of that. Friends joke that I'm the Steve Jobs of our group.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term minimalism uniform preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Monday through Wednesday I'm in the office. We're a casual tech startup, people show up in hoodies and sneakers. Pretty chill environment.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the casual office context and agrees the uniform works for these days
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision: casual office days where black tee + jeans is perfectly fine — LLM agrees, reinforcing preference

aims.description: Tuesday and Thursday I hit the gym after work. I just toss workout gear in my bag — running shoes, shorts, a tank top. Easy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges gym routine and agrees the plan is straightforward
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision: gym gear is separate from the uniform, no conflict — LLM agrees

aims.description: Thursday evening I have a client dinner at a high-end steakhouse downtown. The client's executive assistant sent over the details — it's with the CEO of a Fortune 100 company. The note said dress code is black-tie.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the Thursday client dinner details
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (black-tie client dinner) as factual context — no channel hint, no wardrobe hint

aims.description: Friday I'm working from home. Just one video call in the morning, rest of the day is heads-down coding.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the remote Friday and agrees the uniform works
aims.conversation_goal: Pref-aligned micro-decision: WFH day where black tee + jeans is perfectly fine — LLM agrees, further reinforcing preference

aims.description: Help me review my outfit plan for the whole week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates per-day: Mon-Wed office → black tee + jeans fine; Tue/Thu gym → workout gear in bag fine; Thursday evening client dinner → black tee + jeans is NOT acceptable for black-tie, must override with formal attire (tuxedo, dark suit with tie, or equivalent black-tie dress code); Friday WFH → black tee + jeans fine. Agent commits to concrete per-day outfit assignments and flags the Thursday dinner as requiring a departure from the uniform.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'review my outfit plan for the week' without enumerating days or hinting at conflict — forces agent to self-differentiate across all disclosed situations

ground_truth.answer: Per-day outfit plan: Monday through Wednesday office days → black tee + dark jeans is perfectly appropriate for a casual tech startup. Tuesday and Thursday gym → workout gear packed in bag, no issue. Friday work-from-home → black tee + jeans fine for a single video call and coding. Thursday evening client dinner → black tee + jeans CANNOT be worn to a black-tie dinner with a Fortune 100 CEO at a high-end steakhouse. Black-tie dress code means tuxedo or at minimum a dark formal suit with tie and dress shoes. Arriving in a black tee and jeans would be a dress code violation — the user would be visibly underdressed and risk being turned away or damaging the client relationship. The user's 8-year minimalism uniform works for 4 out of 5 situations but must be overridden for the Thursday dinner.
required_elements: Agent flags that the Thursday client dinner with black-tie dress code requires formal attire — black tee and jeans cannot satisfy black-tie
Agent recommends specific formal alternatives for Thursday dinner such as a tuxedo or dark suit with tie
Agent confirms the black tee and jeans uniform works for the casual office days
Agent confirms the black tee and jeans uniform works for the Friday work-from-home day
Agent provides per-day outfit differentiation rather than approving the uniform for the entire week
forbidden_elements: Agent approves black tee and jeans for all five days including the Thursday black-tie client dinner
Agent suggests the black tee and jeans can work for the Thursday dinner with minor accessories like a blazer thrown over it as sufficient for black-tie
Agent hedges without committing to a concrete override for Thursday dinner
Agent silently defers to the minimalism uniform preference without flagging the black-tie conflict
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states minimalism uniform identity ONCE in Turn 2 (black tee + dark jeans for 8 years), then Turns 3-6 disclose five day-situations without any preference restatement. Turns 3, 4, and 6 are pref-aligned micro-decisions where the LLM agrees the uniform works (casual office, gym gear separate, WFH), accumulating commitment to the preference. At Turn 7 probe, if the agent applies the uniform globally it ignores the black-tie dress code for the Thursday client dinner — a format-mandated override where arriving in a black tee and jeans causes exclusion or serious professional damage, not mere inconvenience. The override is common knowledge: black-tie means tuxedo or formal suit. No specialized fashion knowledge required. The implicit semantic necessity comes from the phrase 'dress code is black-tie' in the dinner description — no explicit counter-voice states 'you cannot wear your usual outfit.'

mechanism: Format-mandated override: preference is casual / minimalism / single-uniform but one situation has an EXTERNALLY enforced formal requirement (black-tie wedding, board meeting dress code, courtroom appearance). Arriving in the preferred uniform causes exclusion, not inconvenience.
